title: Driverless Taxi Cameras Raise Questions About Rider Privacy
summary:
A taxi without a driver may still have someone checking what happens inside. Companies including Waymo, Zoox and Tesla use cameras in their driverless taxis, sometimes called robotaxis.

Outside cameras help these cars notice the road around them. Inside cameras serve different purposes. Companies say they help keep riders safe, check that passengers follow rules, find lost items and check whether a car needs cleaning.

Waymo says it uses automatic technology to help staff spot possible rule violations. Human workers have also used the car's speaker system to check whether passengers were old enough to ride alone.

Zoox says its inside cameras record the whole ride. Its policies allow personal information to help run rides and improve its service. Tesla's documents say a green sign appears on the car's screen when its camera is active. Riders can choose to share inside video and sound through an app setting. The documents say early access riders automatically agree to sharing. Tesla did not tell WIRED whether that program had ended.

The companies say workers view camera footage only when needed. They also say personal information may be given to police or regulators.

Privacy means having some control over personal information. Privacy experts say few clear US rules govern this kind of monitoring. Matthew Guariglia of the Electronic Frontier Foundation is concerned about how much information companies collect and what happens to it afterward.
why_it_matters: Passengers may share personal information during a ride. Knowing how cameras work helps them understand questions about who can view or use that information.
